Sanjay — great to hear the demo landed well.

Quick response and an initial draft attached (redwood_map_draft_v1.pdf). Key points up front:

1) Proposed MAP cadence (high level)
   - Week 1-2: Technical eval (MedCord dev + Redwood tech check-ins) — acceptance = performance & integration signoff (owner: MedCord dev lead)
   - Week 3: Security checklist & SOC2 evidence review — acceptance = security confirmation (owner: MedCord security)
   - Week 4: Legal & procurement review (MSA/DPA redlines) — acceptance = signed MSA or agreed signature plan (owner: MedCord legal)
   - Week 5: Pilot order form + billing & onboarding kickoff — acceptance = PO or signed order form (owner: MedCord procurement)

2) Sequencing advice
   - We can start the pilot onboarding (order form provisional) while DPA language is in parallel negotiation, provided MedCord can accept data processing constraints in the pilot config (region pinning + short retention) — this reduces time-to-value.
   - If your security team requires a fully executed DPA before any PII touches our environment, the milestone for order form execution should follow DPA sign-off.

3) Contingencies
   - If SOC2 evidence takes > 7 business days to validate, proposal is to issue a timeboxed exception (30-day pilot) with escrowed logs and stricter prefixes.

I've looped Laura for legal touchpoints and Grace for onboarding/ops capacity planning. Attached the MAP draft and a concise checklist. Will follow up with a compact timeline + DocuSign link once legal visibility is set.

Cheers,

Hi all — quick legal note on sequencing and a suggested minimums list so procurement has something concrete to evaluate.

- DPA vs MSA: We prefer to finalize the DPA in parallel to the MSA but understand procurement pressure to sign commercial terms (order form) earlier. For pilots involving customer data, our standard approach is: sign a short order form with a narrow pilot scope AND execute a DPA that references the pilot scope before data ingestion. This protects both parties and lets product teams start integrations.

- Redline priorities I expect MedCord to push: subprocessors, deletion timelines, breach notification SLA (we usually accept 72 hours), and data residency obligations. I've attached a short redlines doc (msa_redlines_legal.docx) highlighting clauses that typically require negotiation.

- Suggested acceptance gating language for the MAP (so procurement can see decision rules):
   * Technical Acceptance = successful test harness results + latency under SLA
   * Security Acceptance = SOC2 artifact review + required controls mapped
   * Legal Acceptance = DPA executed OR signed addendum limiting processing scope for pilot
   * Commercial Acceptance = signed pilot order form OR procurement-issued PO referencing the order form

If procurement insists on signature order, we can propose a conditional signature path (MSA signature + DPA to follow within 14 days) with a clause that limits pilot to non-production data until DPA is executed. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk these to MedCord legal.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: msa_redlines_legal.docx (docx, 22KB)
